c: Muramasa creates a series of slashes at the closest enemies. When retaliating, it slashes six times around the character and can retaliate every 0.6 seconds.
Muramasa's Base Damage is doubled and has a lower
and Interval, compared to Night Sword. The
of slashes for each attack is lowered.
Muramasa's damage is multiplied by 2 x
Muramasa has a 10% chance to generate little hearts that heal 1 point of health upon killing an enemy, which is 10 times more than its base form. This chance is affected by
It also gains a finisher, causing every fifth slash to become vertical, covering a large area.
By default, it is capable of dealing critical hits, which deal 2x damage and have 10% chance to occur. The chance is affected by Luck.
Muramasa drains a max of 4 health per activation, decreasing as the player's health reaches 25%. At this point, it only drains 1 health.

Muramasa's ability to drain the character's health is useful for builds that are based on
For example, there is a synergy between it and
; Soul Eater's power increases by healing missing health but enemies cannot reach the player because they are defeated too quickly, Muramasa provides that opportunity to heal up.

The health drained by Muramasa will also activate retaliatory damage from weapons, including itself. This can synergize with Divine Bloodline (IX) in order to scale Max Health even when enemies are no longer capable of damaging the player.
Due to the way it scales with
, Muramasa is a great pick for characters with scaling Greed or high native Greed.
Characters with immunity to Health Drain, such as
, are immune to its health drain, but this can be a drawback as this means they cannot use it in combination with Wandering the Jet Black,
and other weapons and items that require the character to be losing health.

. They were a famous swordsmith and the blades were favored by the shogen Tokugawa Ieyasu, but the katana gradually became a symbol of the anti-Tokugawa movement. Furthermore, in lore and popular culture since the 18th century, the sword has been regarded as yōtō (妖刀, "wicked katana"). Sometimes, the blade is depicted with a blood-red color like the icon. Hence, the blade's curse causes the character to lose health when using it.
The base weapon and health-draining mechanic of Muramasa could also be a potential reference to the magic sword
from Brandon Sanderson's novels. Whenever that blade is drawn, it starts consuming the soul of the wielder.
